speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to assess this newborn presenting with respiratory distress. Can you tell me the baby's gestational age at birth and the mode of delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Was there a delay in the clearance of fetal lung fluid, and did the baby have any signs of distress immediately after birth? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms, suggesting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray findings of ground-glass appearance and air bronchograms are classic for Respiratory Distress Syndrome, especially given the preterm gestational age and maternal diabetes history. Do you have any information on the baby's birth weight or Apgar scores to further confirm the severity?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: These clinical signs of retractions, flaring, and cyanosis, combined with the X-ray findings, strongly confirm Respiratory Distress Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
